Name: whitened_frozen_frontend_codebook
Title: Can a Fixed Whitening Halve the Codebook Perplexity Deficit of a Frozen Filter-Bank Front End Against a Learned Convolution in an EEG Tokenizer? A Seed-Paired Test Against Rank-Matched Noise
Short Hypothesis: Can the codebook perplexity deficit of a frozen filter-bank front end against a learned convolution in an EEG tokenizer be at least halved without training the front end by a fixed whitening of its tokens, and does whitening gain more than rank-matched noise does? Although the codebook perplexity deficit of a frozen filter-bank front end against a learned convolution is read as the price of not training it, a fixed whitening of its tokens closes at least half of that deficit and more of it than rank-matched noise does, which we conjecture is because the encoder cannot use signal directions that are small beside the tokens' dominant modes. Both parts of the question carry a three-way rule (supported, refuted, undecided) in seed-paired tokenizer runs on sleep EEG in which only the front end differs; the size of the deficit, the share reached by centring alone, the token statistics of each arm and a two-seed repeat on awake EEG are only estimated, and the conjectured reason is not tested beyond the noise control. No simpler route answers it: that whitening raises the tokens' own rank is algebra, but whether a jointly trained encoder and codebook pass that geometry on to held-out code usage can only be found by training them.
Related Work: EEG tokenizers embed each one-second channel patch with a learned temporal convolution in front of a Transformer and a vector-quantized codebook (Jiang, 2024) [jiang2024], and when code usage differs between codebooks the difference is attributed to the reconstruction target (Ma et al., 2025) [maetal2025]; (Cui et al., 2026) [cuietal2026]. What breaks this picture is an observation in the project this proposal starts from (unpublished, one seed per arm): a frozen filter bank with no trainable parameter matches the learned convolution's reconstruction loss while its codebook perplexity is 27% lower, so neither target nor reconstruction quality explains usage. Three literatures bear on it. (i) Vector quantization: collapse worsens with codebook size and code dimension (Guo et al., 2024) [guoetal2024]; (Fang et al., 2025) [fangetal2025], and its cause is disputed — encoder drift (Lu et al., 2026) [luetal2026a], sparse codebook gradients (Chang et al., 2025) [changetal2025], or the timing of quantization acting on the latent's variance spectrum, which leaves only 2-5 usable dimensions from a cold start (Zhao et al., 2026) [zhaoetal2026]. The last account was tested by delaying quantization on learned image and speech encoders, never by changing the spectrum of a fixed input; Fang et al. match distributions on the codebook side. (ii) Front ends: learnable audio filterbanks stay near their initialisation (Anderson et al., 2023) [andersonetal2023], a fixed mel bank is not consistently beaten (Schlüter and Gutenbrunner, 2022) [schlutergutenbrunner2022], and in LEAF's own ablation mel plus PCEN equals the learned filterbank plus PCEN (Zeghidour et al., 2021) [zeghidouretal2021] — the normalisation stage, not the filters, carries the gain. All of this is supervised audio without a codebook. (iii) EEG: a linear patch embedding and a learnable filterbank differ by about 0.3-0.5 point in masked pretraining without a codebook and without a frozen arm (Xie et al., 2026) [xieetal2026]; fixed FFT band masks precede per-band VQ tokenizers with no usage reported (Sukhbaatar et al., 2026) [sukhbaataretal2026]. Reported usage numbers: 3401 / 1260 unused codes of 8192 [maetal2025]; 100% utilisation with residual quantization [cuietal2026]; 14.5% utilisation and perplexity 1,862 for EMA VQ at 16,384 codes on ImageNet [fangetal2025]. No retrieved paper (386 records; 32 read in full, all through a plain-text extractor) preconditions the tokens of a fixed front end as an experimental factor; a title-and-abstract search for whitening or anisotropy with codebooks returned nothing relevant, which is weak evidence for a methods question.
Abstract: Tokenizers of EEG foundation models place a learned temporal convolution in front of a Transformer encoder and a vector-quantized codebook, and differences in how fully codebooks are used are usually explained by the reconstruction target. An observation from an attempt to replace that convolution with an interpretable, FOOOF-shaped filter bank does not fit: a frozen bank with no trainable parameter reconstructed Fourier amplitude and phase as well as the learned convolution, yet its codebook perplexity was about a quarter lower. If equal reconstruction comes with unequal code usage, something other than the target and the fit decides how much of a codebook is used. While this is open, it cannot be said whether an analytic front end can feed a discrete-token EEG model without being trained. We ask whether the deficit can be at least halved without training the front end. A fixed whitening, estimated once and carrying no gradient, is inserted after the frozen bank, and full-size LaBraM-style tokenizers are trained from paired seeds with a learned convolution, the raw bank, the whitened bank, the bank with rank-matched noise, and the bank with its mean token removed. The rules, fixed in advance, ask whether whitening closes at least half of the deficit in held-out code usage without worsening validation reconstruction, and whether it gains more than noise that raises the tokens' rank to the same value; outcomes are supported, refuted or undecided on confidence bounds over seeds. The contrast is repeated descriptively on an independent awake dataset. Either outcome is informative: a fixed normalisation stage recovers at least half of the lost code usage, or what a trained front end supplies has to be sought elsewhere.
Experiments: E0 [instrument] Build five front-end arms in the project's tokenizer (`vqnsp_encoder_base_decoder_native`, 12-layer encoder, 3-layer decoder, 12.3 M parameters, patch 250 samples, 4 patches per window, codebook 12,288 x 64, cosine lookup, EMA 0.99, k-means initialisation, batch 32, peak learning rate 1.25e-5 after a 2,000-step warm-up, fp32 on CPU, 16,000 steps): L = learned convolution; F = frozen filter-bank front end (`PureDynFrontEnd`, 48 poles, 8 oscillators, 4 bins, 0.5-90 Hz); W = F followed by whitening t' = s*C_shrunk^(-1/2)(t - m), m and C from 20,000 training patches, shrinkage 0.1, s matching the mean squared norm to F; N = F plus rank-matched noise (isotropic Gaussian noise at the variance where the tokens' effective rank equals W's); C = F with the mean token removed. Data: the project's ISRUC-Sleep (6 channels) and Sleep-EDF telemetry (2 channels) pretraining HDF5 files, 250 Hz, about 55 h, flat windows (SD < 1e-6) removed, corpus order as in the project; 20,000 validation patches held out for the outcome. Licences: ISRUC-Sleep (licence unverified), Sleep-EDF (licence unverified); both are public de-identified research datasets. Manipulation check: effective rank and mean pairwise cosine of each arm's tokens on 8,800 held-out patches. Needs a stub or an install of `timm` (not installed; a 15-line stub was verified to import the model code). The plan with every rule, evaluation point and threshold is committed and its hash recorded before the first training run. Timing: one optimisation step timed at 0.12-0.19 s on this CPU for 2-6 channels x 4 patches.

E1 [descriptive C2] Deficit of the frozen filter-bank front end against the learned convolution: train L and F from 5 paired seeds; codebook perplexity = exp of the entropy of the histogram of codes assigned to the 20,000 held-out patches, at steps 10,000, 12,000, 14,000 and 16,000, averaged; report D = P_L - P_F per seed with its mean and 95% CI, the dead-code fraction, the quantizer's own EMA usage perplexity and the validation loss. Also the positive control of C1 (project record: 397 vs 288 on EMA usage, 15 patches, one seed). Precondition for E2 and E4: mean D > 0 at one-sided paired p < 0.05; otherwise non-replication at this scale is reported and C1 is undecided. Compute: 10 runs, about 6-8 CPU-hours (estimated from the timed step).

E2 [tests C1] Whitening: train W from the same 5 seeds; G = P_W - P_F. Three-way rule on one-sided 95% confidence bounds of mean(G - 0.5 D) over seeds, read on the four-point mean and at step 16,000 alone: C1 is refuted if the upper bound is below 0 on both readings, or if a guard fails — W's validation loss (mean of the evaluation points and the seeds) exceeds F's by more than the larger of 1% and twice the between-seed SD of F's, or W's code informativeness (share of the held-out Fourier-amplitude target variance explained by the mean target of the assigned code) falls below F's by more than twice its between-seed SD; supported on this experiment if the lower bound is above 0 on both readings and the guards hold; undecided otherwise, including when the two readings disagree (a difference in how fast the codebook fills, not in where it ends). Compute: 5 runs, about 3-4 CPU-hours (estimated).

E3 [descriptive C3] Beside each arm's perplexity, list its token statistics (effective rank, signal-subspace rank as in the project's offline probe, mean pairwise cosine) and the effective rank of the quantizer input z at step 16,000, to see which statistic orders the arms as perplexity does. No new training.

E4 [control C1] Negative control aimed at rank inflation by noise: train N from the same 5 seeds; H = P_W - P_N. Three-way rule on one-sided 95% bounds of mean(H - 0.25 D): refuted if the upper bound is below 0 (whitening gains no more than rank-matched noise: the gain is rank, not usable signal), supported on this experiment if the lower bound is above 0, undecided otherwise. The code informativeness of N is reported beside W's. Rank-matched noise also lowers the tokens' signal-to-noise ratio, so this separates 'rank alone' from whitening, not every difference between the arms. Compute: 5 runs, about 3-4 CPU-hours (estimated).

E5 [descriptive C3] Centring only: train C from 3 of the seeds and report (P_C - P_F) / (P_W - P_F), the share of the whitening gain that removing the mean token reaches. Compute: 3 runs, about 2 CPU-hours (estimated).

E6 [descriptive C1] Second dataset: repeat L, F and W on PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery (EEGBCI, 109 subjects cached in ~/mne_data; channels Fz, Cz, Pz, Oz, C3, C4; resampled to 250 Hz, band-pass 0.5-100 Hz, no artifact subspace reconstruction; subject-wise 90/10 split), 2 seeds, 12,000 steps, evaluation at steps 8,000, 10,000 and 12,000; whitening statistics re-estimated on this dataset. EEGBCI (licence unverified). With 2 seeds mean G against 0.5 x mean D is reported as agreement or disagreement in sign and size; no test. Compute: 6 runs, about 3-4 CPU-hours (estimated). In total about 19 CPU-hours (estimated), 4 runs at a time on the 14 cores.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Blind restatement unresolved: the deficit may not be present at 16,000 steps, 4 patches and on held-out perplexity (the project record is 44,000 steps, 15 patches, EMA usage) — budget: 23 runs at that scale cost about 65 CPU-hours; E1 stays a precondition and non-replication is reported.

Blind restatement unresolved: five paired seeds detect only very large effects and the E1 gate is itself a test at n = 5 — budget: 10 seeds for the four tested arms add about 13 CPU-hours; the three-way rule reports undecided instead of forcing a verdict.

Blind restatement unresolved: one tokenizer, one quantizer, the most anisotropic bank configuration and one data pool; the awake repeat has 2 seeds and no test — budget: a second bank configuration needs about 7 more CPU-hours and E6 at 5 seeds about 6.

Blind restatement unresolved: a success shows that whitening helps, not why — budget: testing the conjecture needs arms that rescale selected directions only (about 7 more CPU-hours); it is stated as a conjecture.
Blind restatement unresolved: code usage is not downstream usefulness; no masked pretraining or fine-tuning is run — budget: several hours per run for 5 arms and 5 seeds on this CPU.

Coherence unresolved: the primary claim was not restated after the forced revision (the rule's wording changed after the second blind restatement: step-16,000 reading, code-informativeness guard, three-way rule for E4).

Single dataset: the tested contrast rests on one data pool from one preprocessing pipeline (ISRUC + Sleep-EDF telemetry, with two recordings whose channels are perfectly correlated and three near 1 µV); the EEGBCI repeat (E6) has 2 seeds and is descriptive.

Question narrowed from: Why does a frozen filter-bank front end that reconstructs as well as a learned convolution give lower codebook perplexity in an EEG tokenizer: is the deficit set by the anisotropy of its tokens, which a fixed whitening removes without any training, or by the absence of a trained front end?
Decision rules not externally timestamped: E0 requires the plan to be committed before the first run; if the experiment stage does not do so, nothing outside the repository proves the order.
Rival not addressed (C1): the bank configuration (48 poles, 8 oscillators) is the most anisotropic one in the project record, so the effect may not hold for other banks.

Power (C1): 5 seeds, paired, one-sided — detectable standardized effect d >= 1.11 at 80% power, worse in truth at n = 5; no source reports the between-seed spread of codebook perplexity, so the verdict is marginal and an undecided outcome is possible.
Scope: the conjectured reason (signal directions small beside the tokens' dominant modes) is not tested beyond the noise control; 16,000 steps with 4 patches per window; one quantizer.
